# Recruitment conditioning for the projection

The stock--recruitment component of the OM was conditioned from the 100
historical realizations obtained in WD01. Each OM retains the SSB and
recruitment trajectories corresponding to its SS3 bootstrap refit, with
SSB determined in Q2 and age-0 recruitment entering in Q3 of the
same year [@ICES2024WKBANSP; @ICES2025StockAnnex9aS].

These trajectories were used to parameterize the stock--recruitment relationship used during 2025--2054 and to incorporate recruitment process error during the projection. Differences among OMs are represented through OM-specific stock--recruitment relationships, whereas annual variability within each trajectory is incorporated through recruitment process error.


# Methods {#methods}


## Recruitment model diagnostics and specification

Recruitment structure was evaluated using the historical 1989--2024 series
of Q2 SSB and Q3 recruitment from the same year.

### Functional form of the stock--recruitment relationship

Beverton--Holt, Ricker, and segmented relationships were fitted to the same
historical SSB--recruitment pairs using `FLSR` and `fmle`. Models were
compared using log-likelihood, AIC, and $\Delta$AIC, calculated relative
to the lowest AIC among the candidate models. The fitted curves were also
compared within the historical SSB range.

The functional form used in the reference OM was defined considering
the model comparison and residual diagnostics.

### Distribution and structure of residuals

Recruitment residuals were calculated on the logarithmic scale as

\[
e_t=\log(R_t)-\log(\widehat R_t).
\]

The residual distribution was characterized using the mean, standard
deviation, skewness, kurtosis, and empirical quantiles. The assumption of
normal error on the logarithmic scale was examined using a histogram, Q--Q plot,
and the Shapiro--Wilk test [@Thorson2014; @Punt2016].

Temporal dependence was evaluated using ACF, PACF, Ljung--Box tests,
an AR(1) model, and a runs test. The relationship between recruitment
variability and SSB was examined using residuals and their absolute values
against SSB and the Spearman correlation between $|e_t|$ and SSB.

Potential temporal changes in recruitment level were examined using
changepoint and breakpoint analyses and the $R/SSB$ series.


### Stability of Beverton--Holt parameters

Sampling variation in the BH parameters was examined using 1,000
resamples with replacement of the historical SSB--recruitment pairs. For
each resample, the model was refitted and $a$, $b$, log-likelihood,
and AIC were recorded. This analysis was used as a diagnostic and did not
introduce an additional source of parametric variability into the OM.

### Specification retained for the reference OM

A Beverton--Holt relationship with lognormal recruitment deviations
independent among years was used. The reference OM does not incorporate
Ricker overcompensation, productivity regimes, biomass-dependent variance,
environmental covariates, or an additional process for extreme events.

Variation in BH parameters among OMs arises from fitting the
stock--recruitment relationship to the historical trajectories of each SS3 refit.

## OM-specific stock--recruitment relationships

For each of the 100 OMs, Q2 SSB and Q3 recruitment were extracted
for 1989--2024, yielding 36 historical SSB--recruitment pairs per OM.

For each OM, a Beverton--Holt (BH) relationship was fitted:

\[
\widehat R_{t,i}=
\frac{a_i SSB_{t,i}}
     {b_i+SSB_{t,i}},
\]

where \(i\) identifies the OM, \(t\) the year, \(a_i\) the asymptotic
recruitment, and \(b_i\) the SSB at which expected recruitment
equals \(a_i/2\).

An unrestricted fit was initially obtained using `FLSR` and `fmle`
and used as a diagnostic. For OM parameterization, \(a_i\) and \(b_i\)
were constrained to positive values through a logarithmic transformation
and estimated by minimizing

\[
Q_i=
\sum_t
\left[
\log R_{t,i}-
\log \widehat R_{t,i}
\right]^2,
\]

using the Nelder--Mead algorithm implemented in `optim`, with
`maxit = 10000` and `reltol = 1e-12`.

For each OM, historical recruitment variability around the
BH relationship was estimated as

\[
\sigma_{R,i}=
\operatorname{SD}_t
\left[
\log R_{t,i}-
\log\widehat R_{t,i}
\right].
\]

A convergence code of zero and finite values of \(a_i\),
\(b_i\), and \(\sigma_{R,i}\) were required to retain the fit. Positive
values of \(b_i\), regardless of their magnitude, were not used as an
additional exclusion criterion.
## Construction of the stock--recruitment component in `FLSRsim`

The \(a_i\) and \(b_i\) parameters estimated for each OM were incorporated into an
`FLSRsim` object within the FLBEIA simulation structure
[@Garcia2017FLBEIA]. The correspondence between each OM and its bootstrap refit
was maintained during this assignment.

The model was specified as `model = "bevholt"`, with \(a_i\) and \(b_i\)
constant throughout the projection period for each OM.
The seasonal structure retains SSB in Q2 and recruitment entry
in Q3. The recruitment proportion was set to one in Q3 and zero in the
remaining quarters, with `timelag["year", ] = 0` and
`timelag["season", ] = 2`.

At this stage, `uncertainty` multipliers were set to one, so no process error
was incorporated during the projection. Recruitment process error is
subsequently incorporated into this structure.

## Expansion from 100 OMs to 1,000 trajectories

Each of the 100 OMs was replicated 10 times, generating a set of 1,000
trajectories. The 10 replicates of each OM retain the same biological state
and the same stock--recruitment parameters \(a_i\), \(b_i\), and
\(\sigma_{R,i}\) as the source OM.

Replication does not introduce an additional source of variability. Differences
among the 10 replicates of the same OM are subsequently generated through
annual recruitment process error during the projection.

## Recruitment process error during the projection

Recruitment process error was incorporated annually during
2025--2054. Two parameterizations of the standard deviation
of recruitment residuals were considered.

In the reference configuration, a common value of
\(\sigma_R\) was used, defined as the median of the values estimated for the
100 OMs:

\[
\sigma_R^{\mathrm{ref}}
=
\operatorname{median}_{i=1,\ldots,100}
\left(\sigma_{R,i}\right).
\]

In the sensitivity configuration, each trajectory retained the
\(\sigma_R\) value estimated for its source OM:

\[
\sigma_{R,j}^{\mathrm{OM}}
=
\sigma_{R,\mathrm{OM}(j)},
\]

where \(j\) identifies one of the 1,000 trajectories. Therefore, the 10
replicates of the same OM share the same \(\sigma_R\) value.

For each year and trajectory, a standard normal deviate was generated:

\[
z_{t,j}\sim N(0,1).
\]

The same matrix of \(z_{t,j}\) values was used in both configurations.
For each parameterization \(s\), the error on the logarithmic scale was
calculated as

\[
\varepsilon_{t,j}^{(s)}
=
z_{t,j}\sigma_{R,j}^{(s)},
\]

and the multiplier applied to recruitment as

\[
m_{t,j}^{(s)}
=
\exp\left[
\varepsilon_{t,j}^{(s)}
-\frac{1}{2}
\left(\sigma_{R,j}^{(s)}\right)^2
\right].
\]

The term \(-\sigma_R^2/2\) corresponds to the bias correction for the
lognormal distribution, such that

\[
E\left[m_{t,j}^{(s)}\right]=1
\]

[@Maunder2006].

The multipliers were applied exclusively to Q3 recruitment
during 2025--2054. In Q1, Q2, and Q4, multipliers were kept
equal to one.

Thus, differences among the 100 OMs arise from their
historical trajectories and the parameters of their
stock--recruitment relationships, whereas differences among the 10 replicates
of the same OM arise from annual recruitment process error
during the projection [@Punt2016].

## Implementation checks

Checks verified that: (i) all 100 BH fits converged and had finite parameters;
(ii) the correspondence among each OM, its bootstrap refit, and its
stock--recruitment parameters was maintained; (iii) each OM had 10 replicates;
(iv) recruitment multipliers were positive and finite; and (v) these
multipliers were applied exclusively in Q3 during 2025--2054.

For the reference configuration, it was additionally verified that the
realized standard deviation of the logarithmic deviations differed by less
than 0.01 from the \(\sigma_R^{\mathrm{ref}}\) value used to generate them.

For the OM-specific configuration, realized standard deviations
were calculated by trajectory and retained as a diagnostic. No acceptance
criterion based on exact correspondence with \(\sigma_{R,i}\) was applied,
because each trajectory contains 30 annual realizations.


# Results {#results}


## Model diagnostics and retained specification

The comparison of Beverton--Holt, Ricker, and segmented relationships is
presented in Table \@ref(tab:sr-model-comparison). Models were compared
using log-likelihood, AIC, and $\Delta$AIC. Figure \@ref(fig:sr-candidate-curves)
shows the fitted relationships within the historical SSB range.

```{r sr-model-comparison}
sr_models_table <- sr_models
names(sr_models_table) <- c("Model","logLik","AIC","Delta AIC")

knitr::kable(sr_models_table,digits=3,booktabs=TRUE,
             caption="Comparison of Beverton–Holt, Ricker, and segmented formulations fitted to the historical Q2 SSB–Q3 recruitment series. Delta AIC is calculated relative to the lowest AIC among the candidate models.") |>
  kableExtra::kable_styling(latex_options="hold_position",position="center")

```


```{r sr-candidate-curves, fig.cap="Comparison of Beverton–Holt, Ricker, and segmented stock–recruitment relationships fitted to Q2 SSB and Q3 recruitment during 1989–2024. Vertical lines indicate Blim and Bpa.", out.width="90%",fig.align="center"}

candidate_curve_figure <- file.path(diag_fig_dir,"18_compensation_vs_overcompensation_BH_Ricker_segmented.png")

if(!file.exists(candidate_curve_figure)) stop("Run 05b_recruitment_model_diagnostics.R to create the candidate SR figure")

knitr::include_graphics(candidate_curve_figure)
```

### Residuals and process error

The distribution of logarithmic recruitment residuals is summarized in
Table \@ref(tab:sr-residual-summary). Figure
\@ref(fig:sr-residual-diagnostics) shows the residual time series,
their distribution, the Q--Q plot, and their relationship with SSB.

Temporal dependence is summarized in Table
\@ref(tab:sr-temporal-summary), including the AR(1) coefficient and the
runs test.

```{r sr-residual-summary}
sr_resid_table <- data.frame(
  Diagnostico=c("Years","Mean residual","Residual SD","sigmaR used","sigmaR source","Skewness","Kurtosis","P05","Median","P95","Minimum","Maximum","Proportion within ±1.96 sigmaR"),
  Valor=c(sr_resid$n_years,sr_resid$mean_resid,sr_resid$sd_resid,sr_resid$sigmaR_used,sr_resid$sigmaR_source,sr_resid$skewness,sr_resid$kurtosis,sr_resid$q05,sr_resid$median,sr_resid$q95,sr_resid$min_resid,sr_resid$max_resid,sr_resid$prop_inside_sigmaR_95)
)
knitr::kable(sr_resid_table,booktabs=TRUE,align=c("l","r"),
             caption="Summary of logarithmic recruitment residuals from the reference fit.") |>
  kableExtra::kable_styling(latex_options="hold_position",position="center") |>
  kableExtra::column_spec(1,width="7cm") |>
  kableExtra::column_spec(2,width="4cm")
```



```{r sr-residual-diagnostics, fig.cap="Diagnostics of logarithmic recruitment residuals used to evaluate the process-error assumption: time series, distribution, Q–Q plot, and residuals against SSB.", out.width="48%", fig.show="hold"}

### Parameter stability

Of the 1,000 resamples of the historical SSB--recruitment pairs,
`r sr_boot$n_success` produced fits (`r fmt(100*sr_boot$success_rate,1)`%).
The distribution of the \(a\) and \(b\) parameters obtained from these fits is
summarized in Table \@ref(tab:sr-parameter-stability).

Table \@ref(tab:sr-conditioning-decisions-table) summarizes the diagnostics and
the specification retained for recruitment in the reference OM.

```{r sr-parameter-stability}
sr_boot_table <- data.frame(
  Parametro=c("a (individuals)","b (t)"),
  P05=c(sr_boot$a_q05,sr_boot$b_q05),
  P25=c(NA,sr_boot$b_q25),
  Median=c(sr_boot$a_median,sr_boot$b_median),
  P75=c(NA,sr_boot$b_q75),
  P95=c(sr_boot$a_q95,sr_boot$b_q95)
)
knitr::kable(sr_boot_table,digits=2,booktabs=TRUE,caption="Bootstrap distribution of Beverton–Holt parameters in successful fits.") |>
  kableExtra::kable_styling(latex_options="hold_position",position="center")
```


```{r sr-conditioning-decisions-table}

sr_decisions_table <- sr_decisions
names(sr_decisions_table) <- c("Component","Diagnostic","Reference OM")
knitr::kable(sr_decisions_table,booktabs=TRUE,longtable=TRUE,escape=TRUE,caption="Summary of recruitment diagnostics and decisions retained for the reference OM.") |>
  kableExtra::kable_styling(latex_options="repeat_header",font_size=7) |>
  kableExtra::column_spec(1,width="4.0cm") |>
  kableExtra::column_spec(2,width="6.3cm") |>
  kableExtra::column_spec(3,width="4.0cm")

```

## Parameterization of stock--recruitment relationships

The `r sum(bh$convergence==0)` OM-specific BH fits had
a convergence code of zero. The median \(a\) was
`r fmt(median(bh$a),0)` individuals and the median \(b\) was
`r fmt(median(bh$b),1)` t. In `r sum(bh$b<1)` OMs, \(b<1\) t was obtained.

The unrestricted diagnostic fits produced
`r sum(free$b<=0,na.rm=TRUE)` values of \(b\leq0\). The positive
parameterization used in the OM retained these OMs through the constraint
\(b_i>0\).

The distribution of \(a\), \(b\), and \(\sigma_R\) among the 100 OMs is
presented in Table \@ref(tab:bh-summary). Figure \@ref(fig:bh-curves) shows the
100 BH relationships used during the projection.

```{r bh-summary}
bh_table <- data.frame(
  Parametro=c("a (individuals)","b (t)","sigmaR"),
  P05=c(quantile(bh$a,.05),quantile(bh$b,.05),quantile(bh$sigmaR,.05)),
  Median=c(median(bh$a),median(bh$b),median(bh$sigmaR)),
  P95=c(quantile(bh$a,.95),quantile(bh$b,.95),quantile(bh$sigmaR,.95))
)
knitr::kable(bh_table,digits=3,booktabs=TRUE,caption="Distribution of Beverton–Holt parameters and the historical standard deviation of recruitment residuals across the 100 conditioned OMs.") |>
  kableExtra::kable_styling(latex_options="hold_position",position="center")
```


```{r bh-curves, fig.cap="Beverton–Holt relationships used to parameterize the stock–recruitment component of the 100 conditioned OMs. Lines represent OM-specific relationships, and the black line corresponds to the pointwise median over the historical SSB range.", out.width="90%",fig.align="center"}
bh_figure <- file.path(fig_dir,"BH_reference_100OMs.png")
if(!file.exists(bh_figure)) bh_figure <- file.path(rds_dir,"BH_reference_100OMs.png")
if(!file.exists(bh_figure)) stop("Run updated script 07 to create the BH figure")
knitr::include_graphics(bh_figure)
```

## Historical recruitment variability

The \(\sigma_R\) values estimated for the 100 OMs ranged from
`r fmt(sig$minimum,4)` to `r fmt(sig$maximum,4)`, with a median of
`r fmt(sig$median,4)` (Table \@ref(tab:sigma-summary)).

```{r sigma-summary}
sig_table <- sig
names(sig_table) <- c("n OMs","Minimum","P05","Median","Mean","P95","Maximum")
knitr::kable(sig_table,digits=4,booktabs=TRUE,caption="Distribution of historical standard deviations of logarithmic recruitment residuals across the 100 OMs.") |>
  kableExtra::kable_styling(latex_options="hold_position",position="center")
```

## Recruitment process error during the projection

The reference configuration used
\(\sigma_R=\) `r fmt(ref$sigmaR_median,4)` in all 1,000 trajectories.
In the OM-specific configuration, assigned values ranged from
`r fmt(om$sigmaR_min,4)` to `r fmt(om$sigmaR_max,4)`.

The realized mean multipliers were
`r fmt(ref$mean_multiplier,6)` and `r fmt(om$mean_multiplier,6)`,
respectively (Table \@ref(tab:scenario-summary)). Their distributions are
shown in Figure \@ref(fig:process-error).

```{r scenario-summary}

scenario_table <- sc[, c(
  "scenario",
  "n_trajectories",
  "sigmaR_min",
  "sigmaR_median",
  "sigmaR_max",
  "mean_multiplier",
  "median_multiplier"
)]

names(scenario_table) <- c(
  "Configuration",
  "n",
  "sigmaR min.",
  "sigmaR median",
  "sigmaR max.",
  "Mean multiplier",
  "Median multiplier"
)

scenario_table$Configuration[
  scenario_table$Configuration == "common_median"
] <- "Common median"

scenario_table$Configuration[
  scenario_table$Configuration == "om_specific"
] <- "OM-specific"

knitr::kable(
  scenario_table,
  digits = 4,
  booktabs = TRUE,
  caption = paste(
    "Parameterization and summary of recruitment process-error multipliers",
    "for the reference configuration and the",
    "OM-specific configuration during 2025–2054."
  )
) |>
  kableExtra::kable_styling(
    latex_options = c("hold_position", "scale_down"),
    position = "center"
  )
```

Figure \@ref(fig:process-error) compares the distributions of the
multipliers generated under both parameterizations. Both configurations
use the same matrix of standard normal deviates; differences between the
distributions result from the \(\sigma_R\) values used to scale the deviations.

```{r process-error,fig.cap="Distribution of recruitment process-error multipliers during 2025--2054 for the reference and OM-specific configurations. Both configurations use the same standard normal deviates for the 1,000 trajectories.", out.width="90%",fig.align="center"}

process_figure <- file.path(fig_dir,"recruitment_process_error_scenarios.png")
if(!file.exists(process_figure)) stop("Run script 09 to create the process-error figure")
knitr::include_graphics(process_figure)
```



# Reproducibility {#reproducibility}

The construction sequence for this component is `05b_recruitment_model_diagnostics.R` → `06_fit_SR_bootstrap.R` → `07_build_SR_reference.R` → `08_expand_OM_100_to_1000.R` → `09_recruitment_process_error_with_robustness.R`. The scripts start from the 100 OMs generated during historical conditioning and produce the SR objects subsequently used in the OM projections.

`06_fit_SR_bootstrap.R` generates the BH fits and \(\sigma_R\) estimates; `07_build_SR_reference.R` constructs the `FLSRsim` for the 100 OMs; `08_expand_OM_100_to_1000.R` expands the objects to 1,000 trajectories; and `09_recruitment_process_error_with_robustness.R` generates and assigns the future recruitment multipliers. The seed used for process error is `1234`.

The final objects are `SRs_reference_1000iter_process_error.rds` and `SRs_om_specific_1000iter_process_error.rds`. Deviations, multipliers, and the shared matrix of standard normal deviates are stored in `data/Rdata`, whereas the tables and figures used by this WD are stored in `outputs/recruitment/tables` and `outputs/recruitment/figures`.


# Conclusions

- The 100 OMs were parameterized using OM-specific Beverton--Holt relationships
  based on Q2 SSB and Q3 recruitment during 1989--2024.

- Each OM retains the \(a_i\), \(b_i\), and \(\sigma_{R,i}\) parameters
  corresponding to its SS3 bootstrap refit.

- Each OM was replicated 10 times to generate 1,000 trajectories. This
  replication does not introduce additional variability.

- The reference configuration uses a common \(\sigma_R\) value,
  defined as the median of the values estimated for the 100 OMs. The
  sensitivity configuration retains the OM-specific \(\sigma_R\).

- Process error is applied annually to Q3 recruitment during
  2025--2054, using the same standard normal deviates in both
  configurations.
